model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the “effect” (y-axis, ranging from 0 to 30 with major gridlines at intervals of 10) of six different language models—mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂—across nine language families or categories (x-axis: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, Uralic). Each category on the x-axis displays a group of six vertically oriented bars, color-coded according to the legend in the upper right: light blue (mBERT-L₂), dark blue (XLM-L₂), light green (mBERT-R₂), dark green (XLM-R₂), light pink (mBERT-B₂), and red (XLM-B₂). Error bars extend vertically from each bar, indicating variability or uncertainty in the measured effect. The height of each bar corresponds to the magnitude of the effect for that model within the given language family. Notably, IE-Indic and Semitic show the highest effects across most models, particularly for mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, and XLM-B₂, with values reaching up to approximately 25–30. In contrast, Isolate and Uralic exhibit consistently low effects, mostly near zero across all models. The IE-Slavic family shows moderate effects, with mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ reaching around 17–18. The chart does not sort the language families by effect size; they appear grouped by linguistic classification. No bars are shaded or emphasized beyond their color coding, and no annotations are present beyond the axis labels and legend.
